curriculum.lesson_evidence: Texture is how a surface feels or looks like it would feel: rough, smooth, bumpy, fluffy or prickly. Tactile texture can be touched, like the bumpy bark of a tree. Visual texture is drawn or painted to look like a feel, like dots to suggest a rough orange peel. A pattern is made when a line, shape or colour repeats in a regular way, such as stripes, spots or a repeating flower. Artists use texture and pattern to make surfaces interesting.

lesson.child_mission: Texture is how a surface feels or looks like it would feel: rough, smooth, bumpy, fluffy or prickly. Tactile texture can be touched, like the bumpy bark of a tree. Visual texture is drawn or painted to look like a feel, like dots to suggest a rough orange peel. A pattern is made when a line, shape or colour repeats in a regular way, such as stripes, spots or a repeating flower. Artists use texture and pattern to make surfaces interesting.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A picture of a pineapple has many diamond shapes that repeat across its skin and small spiky lines at the top. Name one pattern and one visual texture in it, and say whether you could touch a tactile texture in the picture.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'The repeating diamonds are the pattern. The spiky lines on the leaves give a prickly visual texture. I could not touch texture in a flat picture, so it is only visual.' The answer separates pattern, visual texture and tactile texture.

WATCH FOR
Mixing up pattern and texture. A pattern always repeats in a regular way, while a texture may be irregular. Something can have texture without a pattern, like a rough stone, or a pattern without texture, like stripes on smooth paper.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Walk around your home or garden and find six surfaces. For each, write whether it has a pattern, a texture or both, and use a describing word. Choose two and draw a small picture of each, showing the texture with different line marks.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

The black and white stripes repeat across its body, so that is a pattern. The short, soft lines drawn along its mane give the visual texture of rough hair. The artist used repeating shapes for pattern and small marks for texture. Touching a real zebra rug would give a tactile texture.
teaching.rule: Use an intentionally weak or disrespectful arts choice as a comparison. Name the specific error, then show a clearer or more respectful choice.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

teaching.feedback: The new example should use the same arts idea as the model, but with different content or material.

teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new artwork or performance.
teaching.model: Texture is how a surface feels or looks like it would feel: rough, smooth, bumpy, fluffy or prickly. Tactile texture can be touched, like the bumpy bark of a tree. Visual texture is drawn or painted to look like a feel, like dots to suggest a rough orange peel. A pattern is made when a line, shape or colour repeats in a regular way, such as stripes, spots or a repeating flower. Artists use texture and pattern to make surfaces interesting. Now choose a different subject or piece to show you can transfer the idea.
